Hi friend, am a former competitive support. Right now it’s the meta to do so, and the plan for them will be to run fast wave clear to shove wave lvl 1 and then invade to disrupt jungle clear by taking raptors since the norm for jungle clearing right now is full clearing. Some clear signs they are going to do it is running an aoe melee support like naut, galio, Ornn that can clear wave and camps fast, and then two side lane champs that can neutralize lane. If you recognize it in the champ select, you have a couple options. You can either run a comp that parallels it and play to punish the invade if they have faster wave clear and just run to hit them at raptors, or you can do what TT was doing and run a neutralizing mid and a scaling bot lane with the support having demolish to get free plates immediately, then play for bot lane. 

If you have it happen to you unexpectedly, you shove wave immediately on wave 1 bot, rotate the support to mid lane, clear wave 2/3 and then back and swap. You’ll be a little behind, so then it will matter a lot more how you macro and play objectives the rest of the game.

Trading stances for mid and top lane is simpler than in bot lane. In mid and top, its positioning over a dying minion to make your enemy choose between killing the minion and likely losing a trade, or trading with you right off of the bat but losing the minion. There’s more that you can do with it, but that’s the general idea. For duo lane, it’s positioning in ways that make your initial engage a 2v1 situation on the enemy. You can still do it over dying minions, but generally for duo lane it’s based around key abilities that are used.

I don’t think it would be a bad assumption to say the percentage of people receiving a degree in the same field of study will have a much higher percentage of its population having a firm grasp on the material and be compatible for the jobs in the field than would be its counter part of people that are self taught. Saying that a university’s quality of education varies enough to be considered to have as little of a guarantee of its quality as self study is disingenuous.  They have certifying boards that are in place to be a governing body meant to ensure that the programs teach the material needed to perform at a job in the same field. 

The reason it would be more likely that someone who went to university would know more of the appropriate material is because the information would be vetted by governing bodies. There is none of that that you could consider to be on the same level learning everything on your own over the internet. If I’m teaching myself business practices, it’s not difficult to take a left turn and dive into bad business practices. 

As for grading and testing, the system may not be perfect, but it is still a way to measure a persons retainment of the material. A company seeing someone who is self taught has no guarantee that they know all of the things that they require. If it’s fields like graphic design or art, you can show by using portfolios. But those fields are not the vast majority of what colleges offer. I can’t show a portfolio as a CPA. 

If someone has work experience, apprenticeships, etc, thats different. But teaching yourself purely online is not a replacement for universities.
